{{Use dmy dates|date=January 2021}}

This is a list of [[container ship]]s with a capacity larger than 20,000 [[twenty-foot equivalent units]] (TEU).

Container ships have been built in increasingly larger sizes to take advantage of [[economies of scale]] and reduce expense as part of [[intermodal freight transport]]. Container ships are also subject to certain [[Cargo ship#Size categories|limitations in size]]. Primarily, these are the availability of sufficiently large main engines and the availability of a sufficient number of ports and terminals prepared and equipped to handle ultra-large container ships. Furthermore, some of the world's main waterways such as the [[Suez Canal]] and [[Singapore Strait]] restrict the maximum dimensions of a ship that can pass through them.

In 2016, Prokopowicz and Berg-Andreassen defined a container ship with a capacity of 10,000 to 20,000 TEU as a Very Large Container Ship (VLCS), and one with a capacity greater than 20,000 TEU as an Ultra Large Container Ship (ULCS).<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Prokopowicz|first1=Adam K.|last2=Berg-Andreassen|first2=Jan |date=December 2016|title=An evaluation of current trends in container shipping industry, very large container ships (VLCSs), and port capacities to accommodate TTIP increased trade|journal=Transportation Research Procedia|volume=14|pages=2910–2919 |doi=10.1016/j.trpro.2016.05.409|doi-access=free}}</ref>

In September 2025, the record for most containers loaded onto a single ship is held by the ''One Innovation'', which carried a total of 22,233 TEU of containers from Singapore to [[Felixstowe]] (England).<ref name='record-2025'>{{cite web |title=ONE innovation breaks TEU loading record |url=https://container-news.com/one-innovation-breaks-teu-loading-record/ |date=22 September 2025}}</ref>

As of January 2024, the record for the largest container ship is held by [[Mediterranean Shipping Company|MSC]]'s ''Irina''-class with the capacity of 24,346 TEU.
